detail: glibc-based OpenSSH server race → potential RCE; upgrade to fixed releases.
Legacy NetBIOS/SMB often co-exposed with vulnerable SMBv1 stacks.
Unauthenticated RCE in Remote Desktop Services on unpatched Windows.
Exposed MySQL is high risk; ensure auth, TLS, no public bind, current version.
Internet-facing Elasticsearch without auth is critical risk.
Exposure only: a file-sharing service (NetBIOS session) answers on port 139. Message signing, SMBv1 and the dialect list were not checked.
Exposure only: RDP answers on port 3389. Network-level authentication, encryption and password policy were not checked.
Ed25519 host-key fingerprint from a signature-verified curve25519 key exchange. This proves key possession on this connection, not known-host trust, host identity or absence of weak algorithms.
RPC portmapper often enables further NFS/mountd attacks.
Public NFS can leak or allow write to critical shares.
SMBv1 remote code execution (WannaCry/NotPetya class). Patch or disable SMBv1.
Superuser + COPY PROGRAM can lead to RCE; don't expose PG publicly.
Internet VNC is routinely brute-forced; tunnel or firewall.
Exposure only: a file-sharing service (SMB) answers on port 445. Message signing, SMBv1 and the dialect list were not checked.
Exposure only: VNC answers on port 5900. Network-level authentication, encryption and password policy were not checked.
Telnet sends the login and every command in cleartext and has no TLS mode.
RMI registries on the internet are frequently abused for deserialization RCE.
Credentials and sessions in cleartext; replace with SSH.
r-services are obsolete and dangerous on modern networks.
The FTP server accepted the user anonymous. Files may be readable, and possibly writable, without credentials; the listing is not checked.
sysDescr.0 and sysName.0 returned by one SNMPv2c public-community GET. Read-only protocol observation, not a vulnerability or authenticated asset identity.

The X.224 connection confirm accepts standard RDP security when no enhanced-security protocol was offered. NLA is therefore not mandatory for negotiation. Login, encryption strength and password policy were not tested.
The RFB security advertisement includes type1 (None). No security type was selected and no desktop session was opened, so completed unauthenticated access was not tested.
The listed security types are the peer's negotiation advertisement; authentication completion and desktop access were not tested.
The server identifies as SSH protocol 1.5, a protocol with known cryptographic weaknesses that no current client should speak.
The server identifies as SSH-1.99, meaning it still accepts protocol 1 connections.
The SSH server advertises key-exchange, host-key, cipher or MAC algorithms that current guidance has dropped or deprecated.
At least one observed SMB negotiation does not require message signing. Dialects and partial assessment errors are retained; relay exploitability was not tested.
Only explicitly selected dialects are listed. MS17-010 is a separate assessment; this inventory gives no vulnerability or patch attestation.

The server answers TRACE with 200 and echoes the request, headers included. That reflects what a browser sends (cookies, authorisation headers) back to a script that can issue TRACE (cross-site tracing). Disable it: Apache TraceEnable off, nginx and most others refuse it by default. Plain HTTP only: HTTPS listeners are not checked.

The peer disclosed host/domain/build fields in an NTLM type2 challenge after X.224 and TLS negotiation. This is unauthenticated inventory; no credentials, NTLM type3 or desktop-session messages were sent.
The FTP server does not advertise AUTH TLS, so logins and files travel in cleartext.
The POP3 server does not advertise STLS, so mailbox passwords and mail travel in cleartext.
The IMAP server does not advertise STARTTLS, so mailbox passwords and mail travel in cleartext.
The SMTP server offers authentication but no STARTTLS, so credentials travel in cleartext.
The SMTP server does not advertise STARTTLS, so mail it relays or receives travels in cleartext.
The server selected NT LM 0.12 in response to an SMB1-only NEGOTIATE. Disable the obsolete protocol. Authentication and known SMB exploits were not tested.

An anonymous IPC$ PeekNamedPipe transaction on FID0 returned STATUS_INSUFF_SERVER_RESOURCES. This is the MS17-010 diagnostic indication; exploitability and patch installation were not authenticated or tested.
The SMB2 NEGOTIATE response does not require message signing. Session authentication and relay exploitability were not tested.
